name: Chaser

origin.basis: Shandong Jiluer Tire Co., Tengzhou, Shandong (brand directory).

manufacturing.basis: The listing does not state the factory.

weight_basis: One owner reported 250 g for a 28C.

availability.note: Sold by Taobao shops in mainland China; no official JILUER store was found.

price_observations.conditions: Taobao/Tmall shop list price on 2026-11-01; shipping within mainland China. The listing does not say whether an option is one tire or a pair.

caveats: Grip was rated lowest in the one owner comparison found.
One owner reports the rubber separating from the casing within 3,000 km; inspect the casing regularly.

An owner of a 25C JILUER Chaser-family tire called it a dry-weather tire and advised against rain and descents; the post does not show whether it is the Pro, so it is not counted as wet evidence. No lab test found.
The listings do not say whether a price is for one tire or a pair.

owner_evidence.screening_note: Checked on 2026-11-03: keyed Xiaohongshu evidence from bounded searches (the first 16-20 result cards of each query, opened exact posts and their visible comments; not exhaustive), coded owner by owner, plus the Sigma Sports and bike-components catalogues and Bicycle Rolling Resistance's test index. Counted only owners who describe their own riding of this model and, where the model is sold in more than one construction, say which; seller replies, questions, unmounted impressions and reports about other models were left out. Reports that do not say Chaser, Chaser Pro or which construction are not counted.

reports.summary: The rubber separated from the casing and the tread wore deep holes in under 3,000 km.
Discarded after 500 km: very light, but very thin.
The 60 TPI clincher had the lowest rolling resistance but the least grip in an uncontrolled four-tire comparison; the owner calls it very good to use.

checks.note: Three posts; seller posts and replies are not counted
